color.$description: NIKATRU light palette. Canonical values mirror the live nikatru.com :root — TRUE AS OF 2026-08-17 AND NOT BEFORE, which is why it is dated. This sentence was here while `text` was #334155 and 14 of 15 live pages rendered #1E293B, so it asserted a mirroring that did not hold and nothing could fail on it: no served page links the generated tokens.css, so the two halves could drift indefinitely in silence. The palette convergence closed the gap in the direction of the pages (the token moved, not the 14), and the one page that already matched this file — the nikatru homepage — was brought to the majority in the same change. Re-read this claim before trusting it: it is prose about two files that no build compares.

primary.$description: Brand blue, USED AS LINK TEXT. Darkened from #2E6FF2 on 2026-09-09 because #2E6FF2 measured 4.49:1 on --card #FFFFFF and 4.23:1 on --bg #F6F8FC - a WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3 failure by 0.01, in the colour every link on the site is painted with. #2563EB measures 5.17:1 on --card, 4.86:1 on --bg and 5.17:1 for white on the button fill.

teal.$description: Brand teal. Darkened from #17C3A2 on 2026-09-09: it is used as TEXT in the .tag pill (2.24:1 on --card, 2.03:1 on the 12% tint the pill sits on) and as a gradient stop under white button text. #0F766E measures 5.47:1 on --card, 4.64:1 on the tint and 5.47:1 for white on the fill. The ORIGINAL #17C3A2 survives as dark.teal, where it measures 7.57:1 on --card and needed no change.

on-accent.$description: The FOREGROUND painted on top of an accent FILL - the primary/teal gradient buttons, the .skip link, the .tag and .trial pills. Added 2026-09-09, the same day primary and teal forked by scheme, because the fork moved the FILL and left the foreground hard-coded #fff on 15 pages: white measures 5.17:1 on light primary and 5.47:1 on light teal, but only 2.69:1 on dark primary #6E9BFF and 2.24:1 on dark teal #17C3A2 - a WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3 failure the light-side repair created. This token is the pair to primary/teal and must fork with them; see dark.on-accent.

soft.$description: Recessed panel tint used INSIDE a card - .note/.plan/.privacy/.c/.shots img, all of which sit in a main element whose background is var(--card). Declared by 13 pages, 17 var(--soft) uses. DELIBERATELY A LITERAL, NOT AN ALIAS, measured 2026-08-17: it equals bg in light (#F6F8FC) but NOT in dark (soft #0E1830 vs bg #0B1220), so aliasing to color.bg would be false on the dark side; and it equals card-2 in dark exactly but not in light (#F6F8FC vs #F8FAFD), so aliasing to dark.card-2 would be false on the light side. It is an alias of neither. NOTE: do not write curly-brace token paths in a $description - Style Dictionary parses braces in ANY string field as a reference and fails the build with an unresolved-reference error. See style-dictionary.config.mjs for the open soft-vs-card-2 collapse question.

positive.$description: STATUS PAIR, light half (train ST-D0, which absorbs ST-Y1). The FOREGROUND tone for good news - text, an icon, a dot beside a word. It forks by scheme because no single value clears WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3 on a light ground and a dark one at once; the arithmetic is in packages/design_system/lib/src/tokens/app_colors.dart. Measured 6.71:1 on card, 6.31:1 on bg and 5.88:1 on positive-tint; status_contrast_test.dart re-measures it on every light Material 3 surface slot of the seeds it sweeps.

warn.$description: STATUS PAIR, light half: the foreground tone for a warning. 6.58:1 on card, 6.19:1 on bg, 5.80:1 on warn-tint. The shared amber #F59E0B it replaces as text measured 2.15:1 on white.

danger.$description: STATUS PAIR, light half: the foreground tone for danger and destructive outcomes. 6.85:1 on card, 6.44:1 on bg, 5.78:1 on danger-tint.

positive-tint.$description: The OPAQUE container behind a positive message (the decision strip, a status pill). Opaque on purpose: an alpha wash composites to a different colour on every ground it lands on, so its contrast cannot be measured once and trusted.

warn-tint.$description: The OPAQUE container behind a warning. See positive-tint.

danger-tint.$description: The OPAQUE container behind a danger message. See positive-tint.
